# Membership of kI₄ is undecidable for twelve 4 × 4 integer matrices

For every integer $k$ with $|k| > 1$, no algorithm decides whether the scalar matrix $kI_4$ belongs to the semigroup generated by twelve given $4 \times 4$ integer matrices.

Use the [membership problem](decision-problems-for-matrix-semigroups.md) for integer matrices.

**Theorem (Halava, Harju and Hirvensalo).** Let $k$ be an integer with $|k| > 1$. It is undecidable, for a semigroup $R$ generated by twelve $4 \times 4$ integer matrices, whether $kI_4 \in R$. Moreover, there is a semigroup $S$ generated by eleven $4 \times 4$ integer matrices such that it is undecidable, for a given matrix $A$, whether $I_4 = AM$ for some $M \in S$ (Theorem 16).

The result strengthens one of Bell and Potapov, whose proof used $30$ generators.

## Proof depends on

None.

## Expansion

The proof follows Bell and Potapov's coding of the Post correspondence problem, with words of a free group represented by $2 \times 2$ integer matrices, applied to a Claus instance, so that the instance has a solution exactly when a product of generators equals $kI_4$ (Theorems 15 and 16 of the source). The proof reduces the Post correspondence problem restricted to Claus instances, whose undecidability for seven letters the source derives from a three-rule semi-Thue system with undecidable individual word problem (Matiyasevich and Sénizergues) through Claus's construction (Theorems 3, 5 and 6 of the source). Neither result has a page on main; a good expansion links both.
